name: Windblown Paper
desc: Loose paper and polythene running before the wind across an empty lot — whole newspaper sheets and carrier bags tumble edge over edge, going nearly invisible as they turn side-on and blazing white as they come face-up to the light, flapping and bowing while they go, with torn scraps skittering along the ground line and a gust front coming through every so often to loft the lot of it.

energy.doc: wind force — how hard the sheets tumble and how high the gusts loft them, plus grit-veil density

scale.doc: sheet size vs design size — 2.2 puts broadsheets right against the lens

density.doc: how much is loose out there (4–16 sheets, 12–90 scraps)

wind.doc: wind direction and strength — negative blows it the other way

hue.doc: paper tone — dirty newsprint cream by default

x.doc: where the light is, so you can tell which sheets are catching it

y.doc: the ground line the paper skitters along and lofts up from

style.doc: aesthetic — newsprint: grubby broadsheet with column rules and halftone blocks showing as it turns · polythene: translucent bag film with a hard specular skating over the crinkle · backlit: no interior at all, just luminous translucent forms against the light · chronograph: a Marey motion study — wireframe outline, four fading ghosts of where it just was, and a velocity vector

act.doc: multi-minute programme — scud: a steady wind walking it across · gust: fronts arrive and loft everything at once · vortex: a slow wandering whirl catches the lot and turns it in a spiral

seed.doc: sheet shapes, tumble rates, depths, print layout (int)
